newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain's Rojo sees CPI key to new rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain's Rojo sees CPI key to new rate cuts.

text.p: New cuts in Spanish interest rates this year will depend on inflation, Bank of Spain governor Luis Angel Rojo said on Monday according to a local wire report.

The Bank of Spain last cut its key money market rate, the repo, by 50 basis points to 6.75 percent on October 3. Inflation stood at 3.6 percent year on year in September down from 3.7 percent the previous month. The government is forecasting 3.5 percent by the end of the year.

Speaking at a conference on European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in the the northern region of Asturias, Rojo said he was "hopeful" that Spain would be in the first group of nations included in the single currency, EFE news agency reported.
Although this was perfectly possible, it was dependent on many factors, Rojo said.
An improvement in economic growth in the second half of the year would help Spain to meet Maastricht's fiscal criteria, he said.
The government has to get the public deficit down to three percent of gross domestic product by 1999 in order to meet EMU requirements.
Rojo said that some still have doubts over the timing of EMU, and continue to call for delays in the calendar set out.
But he added that those counting on "creative accounting" to join EMU will be disappointed.
The political will in European countries backing EMU is so strong that only very adverse conditions would delay it, Rojo added.
